summary: In the 1990s, London housing cooperatives such as Fusions Jameen enabled residents to build their own social homes through sweat equity and cooperative labor. Despite facing local opposition, racism, and demanding time commitments, individuals successfully constructed wooden homes on sites deemed unsuitable for mainstream housing. Today, experts note that while community-led housing remains appealing, increasingly stringent regulations and complex building requirements make such self-build projects much harder to achieve in the UK.
key_points: Tim Oshodi helped build one of 13 homes on Nubia Way as part of London's first black-led housing cooperative in the 1990s.
Self-builders faced racist opposition and rumors during construction, requiring them to guard the site at night.
Charmaine McNally built a five-bedroom home in Meadow Lane through a female-led self-build project and later established her own maintenance firm.
Experts state that modern building regulations, health and safety rules, and funding requirements make community self-builds significantly more difficult today.

title: All On The Board co-creator marks 25 years on Underground with special poem
author: Megan Howe
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/03/17/27/ian-redpath.jpg?trim=544,0,544,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
After years of putting smiles on the faces of London Underground passengers, one of the minds behind ‘All On The Board’ has finally turned the pen on himself.
It comes as a rare bit of self-praise from a man who is better known for writing words of encouragement for other people.
Mr Redpath wrote: “I’m not someone who blows their own trumpet because I don’t own a trumpet.
“But it’s my 25th anniversary at Transport for London, so I wrote this poem for myself.”
Over the past quarter of a century, Ian has taken on a series of roles at Transport for London, from technician to train driver, customer assistant and poet. He has worked at more than 120 stations, helping passengers get from A to B.
But for many Londoners, Ian is best known as one half of All On The Board alongside his friend and co-creator Jeremy Chopra.
The pair began their creative project at North Greenwich station in March 2017, when they decided the usual “keep right” and delay notices could do with a little more personality.
Ian and Jeremy remained anonymous for more than three and a half years, leaving poems, messages and tributes on station noticeboards before eventually revealing their identities.
Today, All On The Board has built a global online community of more than 750,000 followers, with famous admirers including Michelle Obama, Ricky Gervais, Katy Perry and U2.
Their boards have become a familiar sight around the Underground, covering everything from major news events and mental health to birthdays and the everyday ups and downs of life.
When bands and artists perform at The O2, the pair regularly create special themed boards outside the arena where concertgoers can stop for a photo before heading inside.
Both Ian and Jeremy have spoken openly about their own mental health challenges, including depression, anxiety and PTSD, and have used All On The Board to remind commuters going through difficult times that they are not alone.
Read More
Ian's anniversary poem is candid about his own journey.
“I’ve never had the desire to be a manager of any kind,” he writes.
“Because I can just about manage myself and I would never relax.”
He also reflected on the unexpected turn his career has taken, from being dubbed “Banksy of the Underground” to becoming a bestselling author.
“I was called a genius and nicknamed as a Banksy of the Underground,” he writes.
“But I’m just a fella who became a Sunday Times bestseller.
“Working for a living, trying to deal with my ulcerative colitis, depression, PTSD and panic attacks.”
Ian has spoken of his pride in working for Transport for London and everything he has achieved on his journey.
And while he is not considering retirement yet, Ian said he hopes to leave the Underground when that final stop eventually arrives.
“When my train has reached retirement and it’s time to foxtrot with Oscar and say goodbye,” he writes, “I will walk along the platform with pride and into the sunset.
“With an open mind of memories, no regrets and my head held high.”
summary: Ian Redpath, co-creator of the 'All On The Board' project, has written a special poem to mark his 25th anniversary working for Transport for London. Over his career, he has held roles from technician to train driver and customer assistant while secretly leaving creative messages on Underground noticeboards with Jeremy Chopra. The pair's anonymous project eventually gained global recognition, amassing hundreds of thousands of followers and inspiring commuters with messages about mental health and daily life.
key_points: Ian Redpath celebrated his 25th anniversary working for Transport for London with a self-penned poem.
He and Jeremy Chopra co-created 'All On The Board' at North Greenwich station in March 2017.
The creators remained anonymous for over three and a half years before revealing their identities.
The project has gained a global online community of over 750,000 followers and high-profile admirers.
Redpath and Chopra have openly used their platform to address mental health challenges and support commuters.

title: âThe system is brokenâ: Wheelchair user slams train company after he was trapped in carriage as hundreds complain about accessibility issues | LBC
author: Rebecca Henrys
content:
âThe system is brokenâ: Wheelchair user slams train company after he was trapped in carriage as hundreds complain about accessibility issues
Wheelchair user Nathan Rollinson has found himself stuck at multiple stations this year following a breakdown in communications - or a fault with the technology - that left him unable to get off trains.
Listen to this article
Videos shared by Mr Rollinson on social media show the realities of using public transport for someone with accessibility issues.
In one incident, Mr Rollinson told staff at Charing Cross that he needed assistance to get off the train at Waterloo East. They contacted their colleagues to inform them and helped him onto the train using a ramp.
However, when he got to Waterloo East, there was nobody there to meet him and he was trapped on the train for 10 minutes.
To stop the train from leaving without him getting off, he pulled the emergency alarm and wedged his chair in the door to prevent the doors from closing.
Read more: Burnham should cut welfare to fund defence, Tories say as he faces friendly fire in first PMQs
âThen next, the driver's going to go down into being like, âwhoever's blocking the door, get out the way, get out the effing wayâ,â Mr Rollinson told LBC.
âThere were passengers on the train, who could clearly see it wasn't me being at fault.
âThey started getting off the train, trying to get down to the driver, trying to find the emergency alarm on the platform, which wasn't working, just trying to find any stuff.
âAnd the whole time, the doors kept on trying to close on me and my wheelchair and my arm and my leg.â
Mr Rollinson complained about the experience to Southeastern, the train operator running the service, who told him that they had been told he was going to London Bridge, where he would transfer to the Jubilee Line.
Following an investigation, it was determined that staff at Charing Cross had confused Mr Rollinson with a separate passenger with mobility issues who was travelling to London Bridge.
They apologised and offered him Â£100 in compensation.
âItâs honestly ridiculous the amount of times I've had to threaten legal action and get solicitors, and then all they've done is turn around and said âoh, we'll improve, here's Â£1,000, go awayâ.â
Southeastern told Mr Rollinson that âit has in place appropriate policies, procedures and training designed to support disabled passengers and to meet its statutory obligationsâ.
âHowever, on this occasion, the failure arose from an isolated breakdown in communication rather than any systemic failure or unlawful treatment.â
Documents seen by LBC show that hundreds of complaints are made every year to Southeastern by disabled passengers or those with accessibility issues.
In 2025, more than 525 complaints were made to Southeastern regarding accessibility by 258 passengers.
It was similar in 2024, when 292 passengers made 560 complaints.
The top five stations to have received the most complaints between 2020 and 2026 (to date) were: London Bridge, London Victoria, London St Pancras, Waterloo East, and Charing Cross.
Mr Rollinson told LBC that this isnât an isolated incident and is not just with Southeastern.
He said: âEvery day there are problems with disabled passengers and ramps, or just being abandoned on trains.
âEven when you do book, it still doesn't work. It just constantly ends up breaking, the systems broken.â
In the same week that Mr Rollinson was trapped on a train at Waterloo East, he became trapped at multiple points while using the London Underground.
Across one journey, he was stuck at London Bridge, then he was directed towards Bank, where he, again, became stranded, before experiencing a further issue at Elephant & Castle.
Itâs clear that issues with accessibility are not just limited to National Rail services.
Transport for London received almost 1,000 complaints last year regarding accessibility across the tube network.
Highgate Underground Station, Kings Cross St Pancras, and Waterloo were the focus of most of the complaints in 2025.
And, so far this year, almost 50 complaints have been made about St Johnâs Wood.
Mr Rollinson says that there needs to be an âactual response to fix the systemâ instead of just âfobbing offâ people.
âThey have all these panels and they say, âoh, we'll include disabled peopleâ.
âBut, the disabled people they're including are influencers who never have issues.
âOr they've got 20,000 followers on Instagram, so they get a direct response from ministers.â
David Wornham, Customer Experience Director at Southeastern Railway, said: "We are very sorry for the experience Mr Rollinson had and for the failure to provide the assistance he had requested for his journey.
âMr Rollinson's assistance request was mistakenly linked to another passenger, meaning the assistance he needed at Waterloo East was not provided. That should not have happened, and we fully recognise the distress this will have caused.
"Our colleagues support around 233,000 assisted journeys every year and this number is growing strongly. Southeastern is recognised by the independent Office of Rail and Road as one of the UK's top-performing operators for passenger assistance. Their research found that 96 per cent of customers were satisfied with the assistance received at the station."
Mark Evers, TfL's lead on Customer Insight, Strategy and Experience, said: âWe are committed to making our transport network as fair, accessible and inclusive as possible and Mr Rollinsonâs experiences fell well short of our standards.
âOur investigation showed that these were due to an unfortunate combination of unavailability of staff, a separate safety incident and human errors, and we understand how frustrating and inconveniencing these incidents must have been for him.
âWe have made our apologies to Mr Rollinson and learnt from his experiences to make improvements.
âWe are continuously working to improve our network, and through our customer inclusion plan Equity in Motion we have completed more than half of more than 100 actions to make our network more accessible.
"We also continue to work closely with our Independent Disability Advisory Group, with lived experience of disability, to ensure our services meet peopleâs needs.â
summary: Wheelchair user Nathan Rollinson was trapped on a Southeastern train at Waterloo East for ten minutes after staff failed to meet him with a ramp due to a communication mix-up. Rollinson highlighted widespread public transport accessibility issues, revealing that hundreds of complaints are made annually to both Southeastern and Transport for London. Both train and tube operators have apologized, cited policies supporting disabled passengers, and claimed they are working to improve their services.
key_points: Nathan Rollinson became trapped on a Southeastern train when no staff member met him with a ramp at Waterloo East.
Southeastern attributed the incident to an isolated communication error where Rollinson was confused with another passenger.
Documents show that hundreds of accessibility complaints are submitted to Southeastern and Transport for London every year.
Rollinson also experienced multiple accessibility failures during a single journey on the London Underground network.

title: London pubs better than some in the North, says Burnham as he names his favourite

Te dog House in Kennington is Andy Burnham’s favourite pub in London

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/03/9/56/Dog-House-pub-1.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) Asked to name his favourite pub in London, he said: “The trouble is, I've probably been, as you know, in pretty much everyone over the years, because I mean it when I say I love London, and I love London pubs for certain. “I think London pubs are even possibly better than some in the North of England. “You know, you are spoilt for pubs, so I could reel off a lot. “A cracking range of beers, liveners & pick me ups sit behind the horse shoe bar,” it adds. “Local art, curiosities and plenty of cosy or lively spots to enjoy your pint and put the world to rights.” The Dog House was named in The Standard’s “Cosy pubs for winter: 10 of London’s best for cold winter nights” South of the river again. A visit needn’t be cosy, there are more open areas for frivolity and silliness, but there are quiet corners too, little pockets of space that suit soft winter drinking. Behind the horseshoe-shaped bar, the welcome can be disarming if the time is right and to find a seat by the fire is ideal. They were joined by France’s first lady Brigitte Macron and Mr Burnham’s wife Marie-France van Heel. Downing Street said the move would benefit nearly 32,000 businesses across the country and that it would save the typical pub an estimated £1,100 in the next financial year. ![The plans introduced by Andy Burnham’s Government will include measures to protect pubs (Richard Pohle/The Times/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/17/00/7df3e5c0b4399c9ef78e3cd40acb6d07Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg2OTYwODU3-2.85390369.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) Less than a week into office, Mr Burnham stressed: “For too long, governments have stood by while cherished venues have disappeared from our local high streets. title: London Stadium News : FONTAINES D.C. SUMMER 2027
author: We Build Websites
content:
Register for pre-sale access HERE
Register for VIP packages HERE
Having sold out their entire UK arena tour this morning, Fontaines D.C. today announce their biggest ever shows. The five-date run of outdoor headline shows will take in Blackweir Fields, Cardiff(29th June), St James’ Park, Newcastle (1st July), Heaton Park, Manchester (3rd July), Glasgow Green (6th July) and London Stadium (9th July). Support on all dates will come from Little Simz and Viagra Boys.
Tickets go on general sale at 10am BST on Thursday 10th September from https://www.ticketmaster.co.uk/venue/436545
The venue pre-sale begins at 10am on Tuesday 8th September with pre-sale sign-up available here.
Fans who have already pre-ordered Fontaines D.C.’s forthcoming album Dopamine Chamber will have automatic access to the pre-sale.
Fontaines D.C. - Grian Chatten, Carlos O’Connell, Conor Curley, Conor Deegan and Tom Coll - will release their fifth album Dopamine Chamber on 16th October via XL Recordings. Produced by James Ford, it's the follow-up to 2024's UK platinum-certified Romance – and the sound of a band moving decisively away from the guitar language of their early records and into their most seductive music yet. Preceded by lead single "Marianne", the album arrives like a constellation behind undulating sighs of smog: potent balladry, anthemic melodies glinting through the murk. In a world tipping towards collapse, it asks how pleasure mutates amid peril—and what our pursuit of it reveals about us. “The album itself is a dopamine chamber,” says Chatten. “You step inside and we test these different mind- or mood-altering pieces of music on you.”
Fontaines D.C. have spent five albums refusing to repeat themselves – from Dogrel (2019) through A Hero’s Death (2020), the UK and Irish No. 1 Skinty Fia (2022) and the anarchic, kaleidoscopic Romance (2024). Dopamine Chamber is their most radical turn yet. It was made with Ford between London, the English countryside and Palermo, where Chatten recorded vocals in a makeshift booth built from mattresses and cushions. “There’s a poignant sense of us being on the brink of some other kind of form of humanity, or non-humanity,” says Chatten. For their fifth album, Fontaines D.C. have built the chamber. What happens to the listener inside it will be the experiment.
summary: Following the sell-out of their UK arena tour, Fontaines D.C. have announced a five-date outdoor headline tour across the UK for summer 2027, with support from Little Simz and Viagra Boys. The band will also release their fifth album, Dopamine Chamber, on October 16 via XL Recordings. Tickets go on general sale on September 10, following pre-sales starting September 8.
key_points: Fontaines D.C. announced their biggest outdoor headline shows for summer 2027.
The five-date tour includes performances in Cardiff, Newcastle, Manchester, Glasgow, and London Stadium.
Little Simz and Viagra Boys will provide support on all tour dates.
The band's fifth album, Dopamine Chamber, will be released on October 16.
General ticket sales begin at 10am BST on Thursday, September 10.

title: First picture of London tech exec who died alongside wife in hot tub tragedy
author: Niva Yadav
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![](<https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/03/7/38/FotoJet-(12).jpg?trim=31,0,31,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000>)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
This is the first picture of the man who died alongside his wife in a jacuzzi in Spain.
New Zealand native Patrick Tobin, 48, and his wife Thomasina, 51, from Ireland, were found dead in a jacuzzi at a residential property in Cullera, Spain, last week.
![Patrick and Thomasina Tobin](<https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/03/7/38/FotoJet-(12).jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960>)
The first theory is that the hot tub may have malfunctioned, causing “suction entrapment”. This would have resulted in a vacuum effect which trapped the pair in the tub.
Local media has reported that the couple died from “cardiopulmonary arrest due to the extreme effort”, potentially exerted by a struggle after falling or slipping or from battling to escape the suction.
The leading theory is yet to be confirmed and post-mortem examination results have not been released.
Initial examinations also found the couple both had marks and scratches on their body, while there was blood in the water and a strong chemical smell.
There is no suspicion of foul play as there were no signs of forced entry nor any suspicious activity on CCTV cameras of the luxury villa. Electrocution has also been ruled out.
The villa was located on a residential development within a gated complex, just south of Valencia. In photos, the hot tub has panoramic views over the valleys and is described on the hotel operator website as a “ground floor oasis”, complete with a TV and shower area.
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/03/7/40/cullera-hotels.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Mr Tobin is understood to have worked in the tech industry in London, while Ms Tobin worked at the London-based consultancy firm Turney & Townsend as a quantity surveyor in the hotel industry.
Read More
She is credited with working with hotels such as the Ritz. Her father, Tommy McArdle, was a director at Irish broadcaster RTE.
The children are understood to be with an uncle, who flew out after the tragedy struck.
A spokesman for Colina del Sol told the Daily Mail: “We would like to express our deepest condolences to the family affected by this tragic incident at Colina del Sol in Cullera.
“Colina del Sol is a holiday resort that has operated for many years without incident for its guests. The resort has always maintained the highest standards of safety and quality.
“At this stage, we are awaiting the conclusion of the official investigation. We believe it is important to allow the competent authorities to examine the facts and provide an explanation for what happened.
“Out of respect for the victims' families, we will make no further comment. Our thoughts are with the family and all those affected by this difficult situation.”
summary: Patrick and Thomasina Tobin, a married couple from London, were found dead in a hot tub at a residential property in Cullera, Spain. Investigators are examining a leading theory that a hot tub malfunction caused suction entrapment, leading to cardiopulmonary arrest. Authorities have ruled out foul play and electrocution, while post-mortem results are still pending.
key_points: Patrick Tobin, 48, and his wife Thomasina, 51, were found dead in a jacuzzi in Spain last week.
A leading theory suggests the hot tub malfunctioned and caused a vacuum effect through suction entrapment.
Initial examinations revealed marks and scratches on the couple, blood in the water, and a strong chemical smell.
Authorities have ruled out foul play and electrocution, and post-mortem examination results have not yet been released.

title: DNB: Netherlands bank moves billions in gold to London in 'crisis preparedness' move
author: Henry Moore
content:
![Gold bars are neatly stacked on top of each other to form a pyramid shape.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/14d7/live/19860b20-a6e6-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
While much of the gold was sold in New York and then repurchased in London, more than 27 tonnes was physically moved to the UK
- Published
The Dutch central bank (DNB) has confirmed that billions of dollars in gold has been taken out of north America and relocated to London, citing "increasing geopolitical unrest".
DNB said on Wednesday that 86 tonnes of gold had been removed from the US and Canada in a complex operation that took several months. It is now being held by the Bank of England, where the precious metal can be traded more easily "in a crisis situation".
Bank president Olaf Sleijpen said the move was "necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness".
The decision comes amid an ongoing trade dispute between the US and Canada, with both countries announcing fresh tariffs on each other after failed trade talks.
DNB said the transfer, which took place between March and August, saw 27 tonnes of gold bars moved from New York and Ottawa to Zeist in the Netherlands.
A similar quantity and quality was then moved to London, with no need to melt the bars down.
Exactly how so much gold was transported across the Atlantic Ocean has not been revealed.
The rest of the transfer was carried out by selling the gold in New York, and repurchasing it in London, the bank said, external.
"Combining the processes of buying and selling and physical transport has allowed DNB to spread the risks associated with such a complex physical gold relocation," the statement said.
DNB did not confirm what it was referring to with its mention of "geopolitical unrest" but the US economy remains in an uncertain position due to the country's ongoing war with Iran, which has impacted global trade.
Canada, meanwhile, has been hit hard by US tariffs on its key sectors of steel, aluminium, lumber and automobiles as well as an additional 50% levy on about C$28bn ($20bn; Â£15bn) of Canadian goods announced in August.
DNB said that gold that is held with the Bank of England "is regarded as the world's most easily tradable gold," and therefore more readily available in a crisis than if it was still in the US or Canada.
Prior to Wednesday's announcement, the DNB held 31.3% of its gold in New York and 19.7% in Ottawa. This has now fallen to 18.5% in both countries.
The total Dutch gold stock was 612.4 tonnes at the end of 2025 and has been valued at â¬72.2 billion, DNB said.
The bank's share of gold in London has increased from 18.1% to 32.1% after the move, while it still holds 30.8% of its reserves in the Netherlands.
- ![A graphic  shows stylised images of the Canadian and US flags over graphs](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/4b95/live/4a224cf0-a4af-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.png)
  - Published5 hours ago
 ![Several ships sit in a large body of water, with fog on the horizon and rocks in the foreground.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/38d2/live/03a25690-a693-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
- ![Ekibastuz crypto mine. 8 large industrial warehouses in the desert.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/756/cpsprodpb/5c2d/live/88718a80-a07b-11f1-bfeb-dfb02ea642ef.png)
summary: The Dutch central bank (DNB) has relocated billions of dollars in gold from North America to the Bank of England in London, citing increasing geopolitical unrest and crisis preparedness. The complex operation, carried out between March and August, involved physically moving some gold bars and selling and repurchasing others in London. DNB stated that gold held at the Bank of England is more easily tradable during a crisis compared to when it was stored in the US or Canada.
key_points: The Dutch central bank moved 86 tonnes of gold from the US and Canada to London.
Bank president Olaf Sleijpen cited increasing geopolitical unrest and the need to strengthen resilience as reasons for the transfer.
The operation involved a combination of physical transport and selling gold in New York to repurchase it in London.
DNB notes that gold held with the Bank of England is considered the world's most easily tradable gold in a crisis situation.
Following the move, DNB's share of gold in London increased from 18.1% to 32.1%.

title: Just Stop Oil return with Westminster demo as Burnham makes PMQs debut
author: Megan Howe
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
Just Stop Oil activists have launched a protest outside Parliament in an attempt to prevent Andy Burnham from leaving his first PMQs.
Around 60 protesters wearing orange high-visibility jackets sat in the road in Westminster on Wednesday, blocking traffic outside Parliament.
Metropolitan Police officers moved in and began removing people, while a “significant number” of activists are understood to have glued themselves to the road.
Others could be seen holding large banners during the demonstration, while photos show some members being carried away.
The protest marks a return to public disruption by Just Stop Oil, whose last public protest took place in April 2025.
The group declared on social media that it was “back”, despite announcing last year that it would end its campaign of mass disruption after the Government committed to halting new oil and gas licences.
The demonstration appeared specifically aimed at preventing Andy Burnham from leaving Parliament following PMQs.
The group says it is protesting over climate change and the deadly consequences that it continues to have on our planet.
JSO protesters added that one lane has been left free to permit access for emergency vehicles.
They point to thousands of heat-related deaths in the UK following an extremely hot summer, warning that rising global temperatures could lead to catastrophic loss of life worldwide unless urgent action is taken.
“Almost 3,000 people died as a result of the heatwaves in the UK this summer. 1.5°C is locked in,” they wrote on X.
Read More
“There's a possibility of 3°C warming by 2050, with the potential for billions of deaths globally by the end of the century.”
A spokesperson for Met Police said: “Police were called at 12:04hrs on Wednesday, 2 September following reports of disruption on Parliament Square.
“Officers are currently on scene and continue to engage with a group of people, believed to be Just Stop Oil supporters.
“Specialist officers have been deployed, and some members of the group have been removed from the road.
“We are working closely with partners including TfL to reduce disruption in the area for Londoners.”
Founded in 2022, Just Stop Oil is known for its highly disruptive and headline-grabbing tactics, with stunts including throwing tomato soup over Vincent Van Gogh’s sunflowers and spraying orange powder paint onto the ancient stones at Stonehenge.
Sam Burgess, 26, a student from Lancaster, who took part in the protest today said: “More oil is a death sentence: the unprecedented heatwaves killed over 35,000 extra people in Europe this summer. I’m not going to sit by and wait for this figure to include someone I love.
“The government must start protecting its citizens and Just Stop Oil.”
summary: Just Stop Oil activists returned to public disruption by staging a protest outside Parliament in Westminster, attempting to block traffic and prevent Andy Burnham from leaving his first PMQs. Approximately 60 demonstrators sat in the road, with some gluing themselves to the pavement and holding banners before Metropolitan Police officers intervened. The group stated the demonstration was aimed at highlighting climate change and the deadly impact of rising global temperatures following recent extreme heatwaves.
key_points: Around 60 Just Stop Oil protesters blocked a road outside Parliament in Westminster on Wednesday.
Some activists glued themselves to the road and held banners before Metropolitan Police officers began removing them.
The demonstration was specifically timed to target Andy Burnham as he left his first PMQs.
Protesters cited thousands of heat-related deaths in the UK and Europe this summer to demand urgent climate action.
The protest marks a return to public disruption for the group following a pause announced last year.

title: London mayor Sadiq Khan says conviction for untaxed car was due to a scam
author: Jess Warren
content:
![Sadiq Khan wearing a blue suit](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1504/cpsprodpb/d822/live/f901e500-a6ad-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
City Hall officials said the car did not belong to the mayor
- Published
Mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan has been convicted and fined in a fast-track court system after being accused of not taxing a 24-year-old Nissan Micra in what his team has called a "scam".
The Labour politician, 55, was found guilty by a magistrate last month of keeping an unlicensed vehicle, in a criminal prosecution brought by the DVLA.
Court documents show that letters addressed to the mayor about the unpaid tax bill were sent to Gordon Ramsay's east London restaurant and the car did not belong to the mayor.
An application has now been made to the magistrates' court to reopen the case and withdraw the prosecution.
A spokesperson for the mayor said: "This is a scam, which is a crime. It's not the first time the mayor has been victim of a scam involving people falsely stating that Sadiq is the owner of a vehicle.
"Such behaviour is illegal, and the DVLA are aware."
The mayor's adviser told BBC London the DVLA was "urgently" looking into reopening the case, with a view to withdrawing the prosecution.
The DVLA will also investigate the false registration, the adviser said.
The magistrate, sitting in a private hearing of the Single Justice Procedure in Herefordshire, convicted Khan in his absence and ordered that he pay a Â£220 fine, Â£85 in costs, and settle the Â£35.84 bill for unpaid tax on the Micra.
After the mayor expanded the Ultra Low Emission Zone (Ulez) to cover the whole of London he faced a wave of protests, including from motorists who said they planned to register their car in his name - supposedly to make him liable for the Â£12.50 daily charge.
![A general view of a silver 2002 Nissan Micra on a road](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1504/cpsprodpb/cc05/live/a1332b70-a691-11f1-bd13-574b21458a8f.jpg)
Khan was convicted and fined after being accused of not taxing a 2002 Nissan Micra, which would have looked similar to the one pictured
Court records show Khan was prosecuted by the DVLA after the annual tax on the blue Nissan Micra, which was first registered in 2002, ran out in September last year.
The DVLA said the vehicle was spotted untaxed on 24 January and told the court that his name and date of birth appeared against the car on official records held by the government.
The agency said a letter asking for confirmation of the identity of the car owner, which was sent to the wrong address, went unanswered in January, leading to a criminal prosecution on 18 August after no plea was entered to the charge.
The court also sent a record of conviction to the Gordon Ramsay restaurant, ordering Khan to pay the Â£340.84 court bill within 28 days or face the prospect of increased fines, bailiffs, or even "a warrant for your arrest to bring you to court".
The DVLA said it was reviewing the case and investigating the circumstances of the prosecution.
Defendants who believe they have been wrongly convicted of a crime in their absence can apply for the case to be reopened, typically by appearing in person in front of a judge to make a statutory declaration.
Khan could argue that he did not know about the criminal case because the letters were addressed to the wrong building.
Once reopened, he could petition the DVLA to withdraw the prosecution if it can be shown that he was wrongly accused, or enter a not guilty plea.
Alternatively, the DVLA could apply to the court for the case to be reopened.

summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan was convicted in his absence and fined for failing to tax a 24-year-old Nissan Micra that did not belong to him. His team and City Hall officials stated that the conviction was the result of a scam involving someone falsely registering the vehicle in his name. An application has been made to reopen the magistrates' court case and withdraw the prosecution, while the DVLA investigates the false registration.
key_points: London Mayor Sadiq Khan was convicted by a magistrate for keeping an unlicensed vehicle after failing to pay tax on a Nissan Micra.
Court documents showed the car did not belong to the mayor and related letters were sent to a Gordon Ramsay restaurant.
Khan's team stated the incident was a crime involving someone falsely registering the vehicle under his name.
An application has been made to reopen the case and withdraw the prosecution, with the DVLA reviewing the circumstances.

title: Concerns raised over two-day London marathon disruption
author: Kumail Jaffer
content:
![A shop owner wearing a striped apron stands in the doorway of an Italian deli, with food displays and shelves visible inside.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/f128/live/23b855a0-a5db-11f1-ae66-53604efd186f.jpg)
Simi Ghent, owner of Simi's Italian Deli in Charlton Village, said she noticed a "knock-on effect" due to last year's marathon
- Published
Businesses and residents in south-east London are seeking assurances over disruption caused by the planned expansion of the London Marathon to two days in 2027.
Road closures and parking restrictions will be in place during the marathon on 24 and 25 April.
Lord Duvall, London Assembly member for Greenwich and Lewisham, described the event as "an exciting opportunity, but it is important that we get the details right" and said "people need clear and early information about how they will be affected".
Hugh Brasher, chief executive of London Marathon Events, said organisers were "working closely with boroughs along the route to minimise disruption for residents, businesses and local communities".
Duvall said two consecutive days of disruption would have a significant impact on communities in Greenwich, Charlton, Woolwich and Deptford.
He asked how elderly and less mobile residents who rely on daytime healthcare deliveries would be supported.
For businesses, the extended marathon could bring increased footfall, but some owners said clarity was needed on the action being taken to ensure the two-day event is an opportunity rather than a hindrance.
Simi Ghent, owner of Simi's Italian Deli in Charlton Village, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS): "This is our first year of trading so we've only had the marathon once â it did have a knock-on effect.
"People are not used to gathering in the village to support the runners, they're drawn to Charlton House, which is further up.
"The village goes down in trade, they're not drawn here to do their shopping and trade."
![A man in a dark suit and light-coloured tie stands in an office beside desks and computer monitors.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1056/cpsprodpb/2790/live/03515a00-a5db-11f1-ae66-53604efd186f.png)
Lord Duvall, London Assembly member for Greenwich and Lewisham
"We don't know how the local council will support us. It has the potential to work well for us, if we were to have the right support â but we don't have any clarity yet. I rarely get any information about it," Ghent added.
Brasher said London Marathon Events was consulting with "borough representatives and communities" to "identify and understand residents' needs in advance, including access requirements for carers, medical appointments and other essential journeys, so that plans can be put in place to support those affected".
In response to a written question about the impact on local people, the Mayor of London told Assembly Members in June that GLA officers "are engaging with London Marathon Events and borough partners to ensure that, if a two-day format is introduced, it is carefully planned and communicated".
Greenwich Council has been contacted for further comment.
Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook, external, X, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk, external
summary: Businesses and residents in south-east London are seeking assurances and clear information regarding potential disruptions from the London Marathon's planned expansion to two days in April 2027. Local stakeholders, including London Assembly member Lord Duvall and business owners like Simi Ghent, have raised concerns about road closures, parking restrictions, and the impact on local trade and essential services. Organisers and London officials stated they are engaging with boroughs and communities to plan carefully and minimize disruption.
key_points: The London Marathon is planned to expand to a two-day event on 24 and 25 April 2027, bringing extended road closures and parking restrictions.
Lord Duvall called for clear and early information to address how elderly and less mobile residents will receive essential daytime healthcare deliveries.
Local business owners, such as deli owner Simi Ghent, noted that previous marathon disruptions hurt local trade and expressed a need for clarity and support.
Organisers and the Mayor of London stated they are working with borough partners to consult communities and minimize negative impacts on residents and businesses.

title: Cinemas across London will be slashing their ticket prices to less than £5 this weekend – including luxury venues, IMAX screens, and the UK’s oldest cinema
author: Katie Forge
content:
![Group of cheerful people laughing while watching movie in cinema.](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/25130311/shutterstock_1661002084-1-1024x672.jpg) 
In what is some pretty spectacular timing, just as the temperatures have begun to plummet and the heavens have finally decided to reopen, National Cinema Weekend is making a rather welcome return. The annual event is taking place this Saturday and Sunday (September 5 and 6), allowing Londoners and beyond to snap up a ticket to some of the biggest and best new movies for less than £5.
National Cinema Weekend
Established by the film-fanatics over at Cinema First (with support from the Film Distributors’ Association and the UK Cinema Association), National Cinema Weekend actually started out as National Cinema Day back in 2022. It was – unsurprisingly – met with a huge amount of enthusiasm, with well over 1 million people taking the opportunity to catch a wallet-friendly flick. This year, they’ve decided to make the event a double bill, giving even more cinema-lovers the chance to enjoy the big screen without having to pay the big price-tag that so often comes attached to it.
![two girls laughing in a cinema, one with popcorn](https://offloadmedia.feverup.com/secretldn.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/25130559/Cinema-Shutterstock.jpg)
530 cinemas across the UK are getting involved in the action, each of which are offering tickets to a huge variety of films for just £4. From the newest blockbusters to cult classics, there’s sure to be something for everybody to enjoy. And with luxury cinemas, IMAX screens, and the UK’s oldest cinema all taking part in the event, it really is the perfect way to spend the first weekend of the cosy seasons.
Phil Clapp, Chief Executive of the UK Cinema Association and Director of Cinema First, said: “Following the success of National Cinema Day, we’re excited to be extending the celebration to the entire weekend, giving cinemagoers greater flexibility to plan their visits, and the opportunity to watch the widest possible range of films, suiting all tastes.”
National Cinema Weekend will be taking place on September 5 and 6. Find out more and discover your closest participating cinemas here.
summary: National Cinema Weekend is returning on September 5 and 6, offering discounted tickets for less than £5 at 530 cinemas across the UK, including luxury venues, IMAX screens, and the UK's oldest cinema. The annual event, established by Cinema First, has been expanded from a single day into a weekend-long double bill following the popularity of previous events. Cinemagoers can enjoy a wide variety of films, from new blockbusters to cult classics, at participating locations.
key_points: National Cinema Weekend takes place on Saturday, September 5 and Sunday, September 6.
Tickets for participating cinemas across the UK will cost less than £5.
The event includes 530 participating venues such as luxury cinemas, IMAX screens, and the UK's oldest cinema.
The initiative was established by Cinema First with support from the Film Distributors’ Association and the UK Cinema Association.

title: Britain's first black police chief launches Tory London mayor bid
author: Megan Howe; Kumail Jaffer
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Senior Conservative Sir James Cleverly has accused Andy Burnham of waging a “war on London” and promised 'fight its corner' in his pitch for the mayoralty](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/01/6/37/FA_2187.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
He pledged to “champion” the force if elected mayor and argued that restoring confidence among officers would be essential to improving policing in the capital.
Sir James announced on Saturday he was stepping down from the Tory front bench, where he held the shadow housing, communities and local government brief since last July, to run for City Hall in the next election.
![Festus Akinbusoye has thrown his hat into the ring for the next mayoral election](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/01/6/37/FA_2187.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
The Tories have fallen short to Sir Sadiq in each of the last three elections since Boris Johnson stood down as Mayor of London.
Neither Zac Goldsmith, nor Shaun Bailey or Susan Hall were able to overhaul the current incumbent, who won comfortably on every occasion.
Read More
But Mr Akinbusoye says his campaign will be different. Unlike any of the previous Conservative candidates, the former Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC) has no experience in Westminster or City Hall.
Should he win, he will be a fairly unknown entity to voters – but with the Conservative Party only now stabilising politically after years of turmoil culminated in a disastrous General Election in 2024, a clean slate may be what’s needed to convince voters.
“My proposition to London is this,” Mr Akinbusoye tells the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS).
“I’m a fresh face. I’ve not been part of a government in the past, but I come with solid private sector experience, having set up a small business with the help of the Prince’s Trust.
“I come with lived experience of the issues many people in London face around homelessness and the cost of living, coming here as an immigrant and the son of a cleaner, and, of course, with a background in policing.
“I bring a completely different backstory and professional experience across both the public and private sectors, alongside a very clear vision – to make sure London is an affordable home to stay and raise a family, safe enough to live and work, with opportunities in all our boroughs.
“I want London to work for Londoners, because London works when Londoners work. We need a Mayor and a City Hall that actually work for Londoners rather than against them.”
![Mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan said the research ‘proves we were right to act’ (Victoria Jones/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/19/07/6cf18c2a55353082ea87aedde5a23035Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3MTQ0ODM2-2.75224103.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Whoever the Tory candidate is must first overcome an election which will likely see four parties fiercely competing for a place in the final two, rather than the two-horse race that it has been seen since the Greater London Authority’s (GLA) inception.
In a thinly veiled message to the Tory faithful, Mr Akinbusoye says that he is the candidate that can “connect with the story of the average Londoner”.
“I strongly believe that Londoners will at least listen to a Conservative candidate who speaks their language, who has lived their story, and who is all about delivering for them and getting London working for them again,” he added.
Last month polling from Opinium suggested the Conservative Party must put up a “fresh” candidate with strong credentials on crime and policing to stand a chance in 2028.
In the polling, 27 per cent of Londoners said a candidate who had previously served in the last Conservative government would make them less likely to vote for the party, compared to 23 per cent who viewed it positively.
Meanwhile, having no ministerial background would see 28 per cent of voters more likely to opt for the party, compared to 20 per cent who would be more reluctant.
The capital’s housing crisis will be front and centre of Mr Akinbusoye’s bid to win the election, should he get the Tory nod.
“This is not about ambition or ego; it’s personal,” he added. “I was one of those people who was literally priced out of London when I came here as an immigrant from Nigeria and set up my own business. I had to move 70 miles away from London to Milton Keynes.
“Moving back now and serving as a councillor here, it is 20 times worse for young people. I want to build a pathway for young people to be able to own their own homes in London and stay, rather than getting priced out of the city.”
![Sir James Cleverly (PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/12/73e60f122771ab3bdc0cfa665aa84406Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4MTc2ODEy-2.85112572.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Safety is one reason for this – and he draws on his experience as the PCC in Bedfordshire to reflect on his policy of focusing on recruiting frontline officers to “crush crime” – but the affordability of homes is another.
Accusing City Hall of failing to work closely with developers to “build the homes that Londoners want, where they want them to be”, he says he would reform the London Plan and set out a “realistic pathway” for renters towards home ownership.
Mr Akinbusoye has also been vastly critical of the Mayor of London and Transport for London’s record on fare evasion, which is estimated to cost the network around £200million every year. By rolling out more enforcement, he says, fares can be kept “affordable” for Londoners.
With a multi-party battle looming in 2028, several high-profile candidates, including former Cabinet Minister James Cleverly, are rumoured to be putting their names forward for selection amid suggestions that Sir Sadiq may not stand in their way in a bid for a fourth term.
Running against a lesser known Labour figure could make life easier for the eventual Tory candidate, though Mr Akinbusoye acknowledged that lessons need to be learned from those who have fallen short in recent elections.
The Abbey Road Councillor says all three previous candidates are “good friends” who have been “kind, open and honest about what went well and what could have been done different”.
However, the way to win the city over, he muses, will be to focus on London, rather than fight along party political lines.
“My focus will be on making sure London remains a great place for people to live, raise a family, set up a business, and get around,” he said. “I will be the strongest champion for London, whether for a business owner or a young person.
“I’m not going to replay the tactics of the past. My focus is making sure my message gets across to Londoners so they get to know me, not focusing on Sadiq Khan.
“Whether he stands or not, I don’t really care. I only care about making sure Londoners get to know who I am, what I stand for, and what I can do for them, their businesses, their families, and their communities.”
A Conservative Party spokesperson said: “We will be selecting a candidate in due course.”
summary: Festus Akinbusoye, a former police and crime commissioner, has launched his bid to become the Conservative candidate for Mayor of London. Positioning himself as a fresh face without prior experience in Westminster or City Hall, he aims to focus his campaign on tackling crime, addressing the housing crisis, and making the city more affordable. Other potential candidates, including former cabinet minister James Cleverly, are also rumored to be entering the race for the 2028 election.
key_points: Festus Akinbusoye has announced his bid to run as the Conservative candidate for Mayor of London.
He highlights his background as a former Police and Crime Commissioner and small business owner, distinguishing himself by having no previous experience in Westminster or City Hall.
His campaign pledges center on improving public safety, tackling the housing crisis, and making London more affordable for residents.
Recent polling suggests that London voters may favor a fresh candidate without a past government ministerial background.
Other potential high-profile candidates, such as Sir James Cleverly, are also rumored to be seeking the Conservative nomination.
