title: One in six prison leavers in London released into homelessness
author: Connie Bowker
content:
![A photo of a homeless person in a sleeping bag on a bench](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/867/cpsprodpb/c3d0/live/1b71b930-a55f-11f1-a261-635a1ee938ad.jpg)
The prime minister has pledged to end rough sleeping
- Published
One in six prison leavers in London are released into homelessness, according to analysis by the social justice group Nacro, as the Probation Service struggles with what is being dubbed a "chronic workload crisis".
It is part of a wider picture of failing support for people leaving prison, says Kelly Grehan, policy manager at the justice reform charity Revolving Doors.
The government says it is working to reduce prison leaver homelessness and investing in probation services.
Up to 50,000 people in England are so-called "prolific offenders", trapped in cycles of repeated low-level crime, like shoplifting and drug possession, according to the charity.
The majority of those in this group - which costs the criminal justice system an estimated Â£242m each year - have poor mental health, addiction problems, and are living in poverty or on the streets.
"Services just aren't set up for the complexities these people have," Grehan said, adding that for people coming out of prison, it is quite common to be placed in unsuitable accommodation, "exacerbating these problems".
"Many tell us they were released into hostels where people used drugs, when they'd just managed to get off drugs themselves."
'I was on my own'
Half the prison population in England and Wales has an identified drug problem, according to a report by the Ministry of Justice.
Anne-Marie - not her real name - was one of them. She was addicted to crack cocaine when she was first sent to prison at 22.
As a care leaver, she lacked family support. She had had her first child at 16, and was pregnant with her second, which made her wary of being open with services about the extent of her addiction.
"I didn't want to tell them the whole story," she said.
She had not been using drugs while she was in prison but, when she was released, was given a place in a probation hostel in Camden, which she described as a "legal crack-house".
"Staff would check on you, but there was no real support and nothing to do."
Boredom was a catastrophic trigger.
"I cut off my tag, used drugs when I was pregnant, and got put back in jail."
Over the next 20 years, she estimates she was sent back to prison nine times, either being recalled or for reoffending.
Now more than four years clean, Anne-Marie says when people come out of prison "they need to be supported every step of the way".
During one of her stints in prison, Anne-Marie got a place in rehab treatment, which she said gave her a taste of what life could look like.
"I thought, 'I don't want this life any more.' Life off drugs looked better."
'It's getting worse'
Tania Bassett is a national official at Napo - the trade union for probation staff. She has been working in the Probation Service for 20 years, and says it is suffering from a "chronic workload crisis".
The early-release scheme - which aims to relieve the prison capacity crisis - will see an influx of an estimated 5,000 people being dealt with by the Probation Service.
"The crisis we have at the moment is going to be exacerbated, and that translates into less prisoner support," Bassett said.
Some Napo members have said they are being told not to spend more than half an hour with each client a week because they have such high caseloads.
"It becomes a tick-box exercise. You don't have time to get to know that individual or for them to trust you," Bassett said.
Officers also suffer from the stress of the knowledge that they are not giving individuals the support they need, and that they might go on to commit serious offences.
"The worst that can happen is someone could die - and that's a big weight to carry on your shoulders."
'Families can't cope'
Lorna's son Steve - not their real names - was sent to prison when he was 19. He came out three years later, in an "awful mental state".
Steve has autism, ADHD, anxiety and depression, but Lorna said he went on to present a range of new mental health issues, because of the trauma he had suffered in prison.
"I didn't know what to do with him," she said.
All of the mental health support Lorna had fought for before Steve's imprisonment had fallen away. She was told he had gone to the back of the queue.
Steve's probation officer assured Lorna they would help him readjust, but her son "wasn't in a position to be helped".
"Probation are there to monitor them, but they don't walk with them hand in hand," she said.
"Families cannot cope; they want to help their loved ones, but they're very much left alone with damaged people."
Within five months of being released, Steve had reoffended and was recalled to prison.
"I asked him why he did it, and he said he just didn't know what to do," Lorna said.
In a response to the BBC's request for comment, a Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: "This government inherited a prison system on the brink of collapse and a homelessness crisis with rough sleeping having more than doubled since 2010."
They added that the government aimed to halve prison leaver homelessness by 2029, had invested Â£700m in probation and community services, and announced a national effort to end rough sleeping.
summary: According to analysis by Nacro, one in six prison leavers in London are released into homelessness amidst a chronic workload crisis within the Probation Service. Charities and trade unions report that failing support systems, unsuitable housing, and high caseloads trap many individuals in cycles of reoffending and addiction. The government stated it is working to reduce prison leaver homelessness, invest in probation services, and end rough sleeping.
key_points: One in six prison leavers in London are released into homelessness.
The Probation Service is facing a chronic workload crisis that limits individual client support.
Up to 50,000 prolific offenders in England are often trapped in cycles of repeated low-level crime driven by poverty, addiction, and mental health issues.
The government has stated an aim to halve prison leaver homelessness by 2029 and invest in probation and community services.

title: Met Office predicts 'very warm spells' for London in September
author: Michael Howie
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Music lovers brave the wet conditions in the final night of Leeds Festival](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/26/13/d80a474e7e528fe5e0253b7515cd50edY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3ODMyOTU3-2.85562992.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
It predicts "warm spells" in the south in the second half of September, with "very warm" weather possible in the next couple of weeks.
![Festivalgoers shelter from the rain in plastic ponchos as they walk through the muddy site at the Reading Festival (Jeff Moore/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/00/ae78c510e521d749ab25048c3c8b2f4bY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4MjE0OTk1-2.85683116.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
While some were seen flinging mud at each other and playing in puddles, others hid beneath their plastic ponchos as they braved the poor weather conditions.
Elsewhere, the cricket at Lord’s in London was halted by the rain on Saturday.
Bradworthy Common in Devon saw 34.2mm of rain over 12 hours on Sunday, more than a third of the average for Devon for August, according to the Met Office.
A flood warning was in place for Spadesbourne Brook at Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, on Sunday night, meaning flooding is expected, while 15 areas were covered by Environment Agency (EA) flood alerts, meaning floods are possible.
![More frequent and persistent periods of very hot weather are driving an increase in heat-related deaths (Jonathan Brady/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/26/13/d80a474e7e528fe5e0253b7515cd50edY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3ODMyOTU3-2.85562992.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Met Office senior operational meteorologist Dan Stroud said: “It’s another day of sunny spells and showers, a generally bright but cloudy start with sunny spells in the east, we will have some showers from the get-go in the west and they will become a bit more heavy, the odd rumble of thunder is possible.
“A drier and brighter end to the day.
“Monday promises to be the best of the three days, still showers around but a lot less than what we’ve seen.
“Tuesday across England and Wales promises to be reasonably fine with some lengthy sunny spells. It’s a different story across Scotland. we’ve got a band of cloud and rain.
Read More
“Wednesday, it changes, it goes downhill, turning cloudy and wet during the course of Wednesday, particularly across Wales and northern England northwards.”
summary: The Met Office has forecasted warm spells in the south and potentially very warm weather in London during September. This follows a period of heavy rain and poor weather conditions that disrupted events like cricket at Lord's and music festivals, while prompting flood warnings and alerts in certain areas. Looking ahead, weather conditions are expected to vary, with some fine days followed by cloudier and wetter weather mid-week.
key_points: The Met Office predicts very warm weather and warm spells for the south in September.
Recent heavy rainfall led to a flood warning at Spadesbourne Brook and 15 flood alerts.
Poor weather conditions and rain disrupted events, including cricket at Lord's and festivalgoers at Reading and Leeds.
Devon's Bradworthy Common recorded 34.2mm of rain over a 12-hour period on Sunday.
Weather conditions are forecast to fluctuate, starting with brighter spells before turning cloudy and wet by Wednesday.

title: London to host two-day 'Dollyfest' in honour of late singer
author: Megan Howe
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Olivia Rodrigo, Sarah McLachlan honor Dolly Parton at Daisy Chain](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/28/12/860f462676a2444c98c8bd3b1a12ef9dY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3OTk4Mjc5-2.20308097.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
Tributes have since poured in for the country music legend, whose larger-than-life personality and philanthropy made her an icon far beyond country music.
According to a press release shared on Monday, the festival was originally scheduled to take place in January 2026 – around Parton’s 80th birthday – and was going to feature her as a performer and host.
However, it will now serve as a celebration of her legacy.
“We had the venue booked and we had the announcement ready to go. And then, in August 2025, Dolly had to take a step back after her initial health challenges.
“A lot of people always say, WWDD (What Would Dolly Do?), and, well, at this moment, Dollyfest is WDWD (What Dolly Would Do!),” organiser Danny Nozell, founder and chief executive of CTK Enterprises, said in a statement.
Her estate added: “We are not discouraging people from celebrating Dolly in the ways they choose. However, as far as a traditional memorial goes, that is not something Dolly wanted.
“So, instead, it feels more appropriate for us to take a beat, let all the tributes that immediately make sense occur naturally, and then, see through this festival-style concept that was truly dreamed up by Dolly.
Read More
“This is something that is authentic to her, something that feels right to me, and something that artists and fans around the world can participate in, while also giving everyone time to grieve, and giving everyone time to plan.”
The announcement comes on the same day the Jolene singer was buried at Woodlawn Memorial Park And Mausoleum in Tennessee, reportedly alongside her late husband Carl Dean.
![Dolly Parton has been laid to rest following a private family funeral (Yui Mok/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/14/5c50d01176bc1dee03c4830ffe1b2237Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4MjY4Mjg1-2.20308103.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Parton’s great-niece, Lainey Parton, said in a post about the funeral on Instagram: “This is a really hard post for me to make. I wanted to wait until after my granny was laid to rest yesterday before I tried to put any of this into words.
“From the time I was little, my granny always had a way of making me feel like I was enough. She never made my dreams feel too big or made me feel like I couldn’t do something. She believed in me before I even knew how to believe in myself.
“Most people can think of at least one bad memory with everyone in their family. I honestly can’t think of one with her.
“Because she couldn’t have kids of her own, she always made us feel like we were hers. She loved us that way, and I’ll forever be grateful for that.”
Images posted of her final resting place by US NewsChannel 5 Nashville reporter Amelia Young showed a brown memorial with a picture of a wooden home in the mountains surrounded by flowers, along with a book to leave messages of condolence.
The singer and philanthropist was best known for her genre-defining hits including 9 To 5, I Will Always Love You and Jolene.
She had already postponed her six-date run at the Colosseum Theatre at Caesars Palace from December 2025 to deal with “health challenges”.
Born in 1946, the iconic American singer-songwriter, actress and humanitarian became one of the most beloved entertainment figures in the world.
Widely considered to be the Queen of Country, Parton was known for her glamorous outfits featuring thousands of rhinestones, her impressive wigs, heavy makeup and form-fitting jumpsuits.
![Dolly Parton died on August 25 (Yui Mok/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/28/12/328b63ab162eb0ce248ea9ed5d835101Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg3OTk4MzE5-2.5404737.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
She was deeply associated with Nashville throughout her career and was inducted into its Songwriters Hall Of Fame in 1986.
Over the course of her career, which spanned more than 60 years, Parton sold more than 100 million records worldwide and wrote more than 3,000 songs.
Following her death last week, a number of Parton’s records re-entered the UK charts, including Jolene, which featured at number nine in the singles chart on Friday.
Since her death, an airport in Nashville in Tennessee proposed changing its name in honour of the singer.
A musical about her life – Dolly: A True Original Musical – will also be launched next year on what would have been her 81st birthday.
A museum called Dolly’s Life Of Many Colours, referencing her 1971 song and album Coat Of Many Colours, is also due to open in Nashville this autumn.
Performers, ticket information and dates for DollyFest are yet to be announced.
summary: London is set to host a two-day festival called 'Dollyfest' to celebrate the legacy of the late country music legend Dolly Parton. Originally planned as a live event for her 80th birthday, the festival will now honor her memory following her death in August 2025. Her estate noted that the festival aligns with Parton's vision instead of a traditional memorial.
key_points: London will host a two-day 'Dollyfest' as a celebration of Dolly Parton's legacy.
The festival was originally conceived with Parton as a performer and host for around her 80th birthday.
Parton passed away on August 25, 2025, and was laid to rest at Woodlawn Memorial Park And Mausoleum in Tennessee.
Her estate and organizers stated that the festival-style concept reflects what Parton wanted instead of a traditional memorial.

title: Man dies after entering canal as Notting Hill Carnival ends with 560 arrests
author: Megan Howe; Niva Yadav
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) ![Dazzling costumes and street style: The best outfits from Notting Hill Carnival](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/16/01M1C6PT6BKGQZ36EVET507YPA.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75) ![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png) A short time later, police said he entered the water near Meanwhile Gardens. Officers and members of the public pulled him from the water and administered CPR. He was taken to a central London hospital, where he was pronounced dead at 4.43pm. Enquiries are ongoing to inform his family. As of 8.30pm, there had been 315 arrests on Monday, bringing the total number of arrests over the two-day operation to 560. Police said the number is likely to rise slightly while later arrests are processed, with a confirmatory update to be provided in the morning. ![

Performers during Notting Hill Carnival 2026

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/16/01M1C6KAMR1JSP29JBBGV7JGCE.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) Commenting on the death, Commander Smart said: “This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are with the loved ones of the man who has lost his life. “Any death following contact with the police is passed to the Independent Office for Police Conduct so the circumstances can be fully investigated. I would encourage everyone to avoid speculation while this work takes place. “I acknowledge the efforts of the officers and members of the public who entered the canal to rescue this man. I know they will be devastated that his life couldn’t ultimately be saved.” A sea of colour swept through Notting Hill on Monday, with performers dressed in bejewelled bikini-style costumes, towering feathered backpieces and elaborate headdresses adorned with sequins and beads. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/21/01M1C6RAWY5RB7SM7K0KCS1F63.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) Masqueraders danced their way along the parade route to the thunder of drums, while sound systems kept crowds moving throughout the day. Read More Monday also brought a huge Latin American presence to the streets, with samba schools and Brazilian bloco bands joining the celebrations alongside the Caribbean sounds and traditions at the heart of Carnival. Percussion groups and drum queens helped get the party started as performers and revellers transformed the streets into one giant dance floor. Police said Shawn was last seen just before 5pm on Wedlake Street, near Kensal Road. He is described as black, 3ft 8in, and was wearing black shorts, a black top and a hat. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/21/01M1C6MYY6B7X6R9ME6YJ3A9P1.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) Commander Charmain Brenyah said: “We are becoming increasingly concerned for Shawn’s welfare due to his young age. “Notting Hill Carnival is an extremely large and busy event, and officers are carrying out extensive inquiries to find Shawn and reunite him with his family as quickly as possible. “We are asking anyone who has seen Shawn, or who has any information about where he may be, to contact police immediately.” Of the arrests made on Monday, 48 followed identifications using live facial recognition. Use of the technology allowed officers to stop 43 registered sex offenders to ensure they were complying with licence conditions. Three were arrested for breaching those conditions, in addition to three arrested for breaches on Sunday. Stop and search was used extensively, with 62 weapons seized across both days, including a handgun during the afternoon on Monday. There were two assaults with knives – one stabbing and one slashing – neither of which resulted in life-threatening injuries. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/21/01M1C6JNRJ8W64AASQ9N6JSVMV.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) The annual carnival is Europe’s biggest street party and billed by organisers as “the greatest community-led event on the planet”. One carnival-goer, named Michael, said: “Carnival is actually an important part of the culture of London, it’s honestly where everyone can come and have fun. “No matter who you are, no matter your disability, no matter your race, no matter any background, you can come here and have fun and you’re going to meet people here that are going to make you feel welcome.” On social media, Carnival-goers celebrated the “camaraderie, advocacy, and profound history” of the event. Footage shared online showed one first-time attendee getting into the spirit of Carnival, dancing through the streets and blowing a whistle as a dancehall version of Angie Stone’s 2001 hit Wish I Didn’t Miss You played in the background. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/21/01M1C6KV2QJED04G8GDJ4957DJ.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) Elsewhere, regular attendees reflected on what Carnival means to them. For many, they said, it is more than just a giant street party, it is a melting pot of cultures and a celebration of diversity, community and inclusion. Councillor Elizabeth Campbell, leader of Kensington and Chelsea Council, said: “It’s been so much fun being out celebrating Notting Hill Carnival’s 60th anniversary with everyone who has come together to enjoy this incredible event. “The costumes, the music and the atmosphere are fantastic, and it’s a real reminder of what makes carnival so special. “I want to pay tribute to our officers, the organisers and partners who have worked so closely together to make this milestone celebration happen. “I hope everyone has a fantastic, safe and happy carnival.” Born out of resistance to racism and racial injustice, Notting Hill Carnival has grown into one of the world’s biggest street festivals while continuing to champion Caribbean culture and London’s minority communities. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/21/01M1C6NCH19QAVFQ8S9GMKAVQN.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) At 3pm, a 72-second moment of reflection was observed for the 72-people who were killed in the Grenfell Tower fire. Sunday’s Families and Children’s Day had brought a more relaxed atmosphere to the streets, with younger performers taking centre stage. Despite 243 arrests over the weekend by the end of Sunday, the Metropolitan Police said the mood at Carnival had been “overwhelmingly positive and celebratory”. Last week, the force said more than 7,000 officers would be deployed to west London over the bank holiday weekend. The carnival, which is celebrating its 60th anniversary this year, includes parades, live music, street food and sound stages. In 2025, the Met said it made 528 arrests across the two main days of the carnival, including 167 for drug offences, 50 for possession of an offensive weapon, 21 for sexual offences, four for violence with injury and 49 for other violence. In 2024, there were eight stabbings, including the murder of 32-year-old mother Cher Maximen, with the same number the previous year, and seven including a murder in 2022.
summary: The Notting Hill Carnival concluded with a tragic incident as a man died after entering a canal, despite rescue efforts by police and members of the public. Over the two-day event, police recorded a total of 560 arrests alongside the seizure of 62 weapons, including a handgun. Meanwhile, celebrations marked the carnival's 60th anniversary with parades, music, and a 72-second moment of reflection for the victims of the Grenfell Tower fire.
key_points: A man was pulled from a canal near Meanwhile Gardens and pronounced dead at a central London hospital.
The two-day policing operation resulted in 560 arrests.
Authorities seized 62 weapons across both days, which included a handgun and knives.
The event marked its 60th anniversary with parades, performances, and a moment of reflection for Grenfell Tower victims.

title: Notting Hill Carnival parade lights up west London as thousands party - live updates
author: Niva Yadav; Matt Watts; Shaun Wilson; Michael Howie; Megan Howe
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) ![Standard on the Street: Notting Hill Carnival edition](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/13/01M1BPKCJWKG97FMBHGSZT39WT.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75) Notting Hill Carnival’s main parade is in full gear with thousands of revellers partying in west London. It comes as the Met Police said the mood during yesterday’s family day was “overwhelmingly positive and celebratory”. Commander Claire Smart, who is in charge of the policing operation, said organisers have "stepped forward" across the event, including better crowd management, after City Hall gave an extra £4.6 million to double the number of stewards and improve the use of CCTV cameras along the parade's route. The Standard will keep you updated on all the Carnival news and colour as the party heats up. Scroll down for the latest updates... Live updates What Notting Hill Carnival means to London Notting Hill Carnival 2026 is almost over! As the party draws to a close, we take a look at what Carnival means to Londoners. Beyond being one giant dance floor, it’s a melting pot of cultures, celebrating diversity and inclusivity. Born out of resistance to racial injustices, the Carnival continues to be a champion for Caribbean and minority cultures. It’s one of a kind and an event that is truly iconic to London. ![Standard on the Street: Notting Hill Carnival edition](https://cdn.ex.co/transformations-account/production/761715bb-261d-4032-af09-a493a82bd926/34beda25-8e8f-40b3-8fff-35fa23f5a2e4/thumbnail-360.webp) What is a drum queen? Did you spot the drum queen? Drum queens, or rainha da baterias, are integral parts of samba schools. They are the lead female dancers and usually parade in front of the percussion section. Notting Hill Carnival embraces Brazilian bloca bands and samba schools, in addition to celebrating its Caribbean roots. Watch: The best bits of the Adult's Day Parade Monday’s Adult’s Day Parade saw hundreds of masqueraders dance their way through Notting Hill. There was a massive Latin American presence on Monday, as is routine for Adult’s Day, while Sunday leans closer to Carnival’s Caribbean roots. Samba schools and Brazilian bloco bands got the party started with percussion groups and drum-queens. Sounds of the Caribbean weren’t far behind and soon, the streets were alive with soca music and dancehall anthems. With feather backpacks in tow, masqueraders celebrated Notting Hill Carnival to the fullest. ![Notting Hill Carnival 2026: Best bits of Adult's Day Parade](https://cdn.ex.co/transformations-account/production/761715bb-261d-4032-af09-a493a82bd926/440e19b3-4cc6-4c32-9867-c3a4cee0af29/thumbnail-360.webp) First time at Carnival was 'a jump' Social media users have celebrated the “camaraderie, advocacy, and profound history” at Notting Hill Carnival on bank holiday Monday. Footage shows a first-timer at the event grooving in the streets of Notting Hill, blowing a whistle as a dancehall version of Angie Stone’s 2001 hit “Wish I Didn’t Miss You” blares in the background. What is a sound system? Sound systems are an integral part of Carnival and they keep the party going until 7pm when things start to wind down. Right now, the streets are rocking with dancehall, reggae, and soca blaring through W10. Yesterday saw thousands flock to the mobile DJ booths dotted around the Carnival footprint. Hits - like Gaza Slim’s Everything Fi Hold Him - kept the party alive just a little longer. ![Notting Hill Carnival 2026: Time to party at Notting Hill Carnival](https://cdn.ex.co/transformations-account/production/761715bb-261d-4032-af09-a493a82bd926/38d59ed8-ac56-4703-98f8-def6a1e59ab3/thumbnail-360.webp) In pictures: Notting Hill Carnival Carnival isn’t over yet, but we’ve rounded up some of the best moments from Europe’s largest street party. Check out all the best photos and videos from this iconic event here: ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/14/01M19DRAKSYXCY2DFRAFHKQF03.jpg?width=960&auto=webp&quality=75) Notting Hill Carnival’s mas bands passed the baton onto the next generation on Family Day Where to go after Notting Hill Carnival Notting Hill Carnival winds down from 7pm as sound systems and bands are all bound to strict sound restrictions imposed by the council. But the party doesn’t have to stop there. You’ll only need to take a short walk through Notting Hill to find a pub or bar waiting to welcome carnival-goers. Otherwise, there are plenty of places across the capital hosting afterparties. Even for Londoners who didn’t attend Carnival, you can join in on the action at an afterparty. Find out more here: ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2025/08/25/8/23/Notting-Hill-Carnival-2025-uarnkbof.jpeg?width=960&auto=webp&quality=75) From your first dance to your last, The Standard has your guide to all the after parties and sound systems at Notting Hill Carnival How many arrests at Notting Hill Carnival? The number of arrests at Notting Hill Carnival has not yet been released by the Met Police. But yesterday’s mood was hailed as “overwhelmingly positive and celebratory”. There has been an update to the number of arrests, with the Met Police now confirming that 243 people were arrested. There has been a palpable police presence across the Carnival footprint, keeping spectators and masqueraders safe. ![

Police officers man portable walk through metal detectors

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/16/01M19KKCVMX4N2T4SKW2HS618Q.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Sounds of soca and drumming echoing through Portobello Road The sounds of steel pans, drumming, and soca music are still going strong in W10. On Portobello Road, music is keeping the party alive, even as the parade draws to a close. Drinks are still flowing as revellers continue to celebrate Caribbean culture late into Monday afternoon. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/31/17/01M1C6H8CZ5X8H3W2XGZDK44H9.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Crowds still soaking up the party Footage shared on social media shows crowds are still filling the streets of Notting Hill. Music is still blaring in the background, while revellers enjoy drinks and soak in the party atmosphere.
summary: Thousands of revellers participated in the Notting Hill Carnival parade in west London, celebrating Caribbean culture, diversity, and music. The Met Police reported that the mood during the event was overwhelmingly positive and celebratory, with 243 arrests ultimately confirmed. Organisers improved crowd management and stewarding following additional funding from City Hall.
key_points: The Met Police confirmed a total of 243 arrests during the event.
City Hall provided an extra £4.6 million to double stewards and improve CCTV coverage along the route.
Monday's Adult's Day featured samba schools, Latin American bands, soca music, and dancehall anthems.
The Carnival serves as an iconic celebration of Caribbean and minority cultures in London.

title: London transport upholstery becomes Mastermind specialist subject
author: Jess Warren
content:
![Emily Medhurst in a Transport for London moquette-inspired knitted vest on a black leather Mastermind seat in a studio.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/daf5/live/9407b680-a1fc-11f1-a97e-999c5aae08bf.jpg)
Emily Medhurst appeared on Mastermind in a vest she had knitted in the style of the London Overground moquette
- Published
A woman who competed on Mastermind with Transport for London's (TfL) patterned upholstery as her specialist subject has said she is glad to see more people appreciating "beautiful design in public life".
Emily Medhurst said she chose to specialise in London's moquette, a durable, woollen seating material that is used in upholstery on public transport across the world, as she grew up in the capital and had "always been interested in textiles and design".
She appeared on the BBC quiz show wearing a vest that she had knitted that featured the London Overground moquette designed by Wallace Sewell.
Medhurst scored eight points on her chosen subject and came third during the episode of Mastermind.
![The interior of a Tube carriage on the Bakerloo line in London. The seats have a distinctive patterned fabric of blue and red.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/bcf3/live/4d3afa10-a1fb-11f1-a97e-999c5aae08bf.jpg)
In the 1930s, textile designers were commissioned by London Transport to produce exclusive moquette designs
She said it took approximately 100 hours to make the moquette-inspired garment, adding: "I just love the colours. It was a bit of a labour of love."
Medhurst said that as a child, she would regularly watch Mastermind, Only Connect and University Challenge.
"I'm not at university, and I didn't have two other people, so I thought 'I guess I'll have to do Mastermind'," she said of her decision to apply for the show.
The Londoner added that growing up, she was given 10p from her mother for every correct answer she gave while watching University Challenge.
"We would tally that up over the whole season."
![A Central line Tube carriage with blue and red fabric seating.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1680/cpsprodpb/e1d2/live/b8eeb170-a1fb-11f1-a97e-999c5aae08bf.jpg)
The moquette on the Central line, from 2010, features four London landmarks
On her choice of specialist subject, she said: "I've always been interested in textiles and design. I grew up in London and loved the Tube and the design that is part of TfL.
"I love public transport, I think everyone should have access to it.
"I went to an open day at Acton depot a couple of years ago and they had a stand there about moquette.
"It was the perfect marriage of my interests."
Medhurst accepted that she "probably knew more than the average person" when it came to the woven fabric, but added: "Going on Mastermind was a really good excuse to delve into the topic.
"There was a lot of revision leading up [to it]. I wasn't too nervous until the week before and then it really hit that I was actually going to be on the show."
She explained how she used books to revise the designs and their history, alongside the "really great" archive from the London Transport Museum.
![Purple patterned chairs on an Elizabeth Line train.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/02c8/live/0b5582e0-a1fc-11f1-a97e-999c5aae08bf.jpg)
The purple Elizabeth Line moquette was designed by Wallace Sewell in 2015
Asked what made a good moquette, Medhurst said the fabric should have "a unique design, good use of colour and a good identity to the line or what it was representing".
"If you've lived in London or travelled in London, you've obviously seen it," she added.
"I think it's cool that in a time where we want to make everything cheap, easy and plain, people are noticing this thing that is beautiful design in public life."

summary: Emily Medhurst appeared on the BBC quiz show Mastermind with Transport for London's moquette upholstery as her specialist subject. During the episode, she wore a handmade vest knitted in the style of the London Overground moquette, which took about 100 hours to make. Medhurst scored eight points on her chosen topic and finished in third place.
key_points: Emily Medhurst chose London transport moquette as her specialist subject on Mastermind.
She wore a self-knitted vest featuring the London Overground moquette designed by Wallace Sewell.
Medhurst scored eight points on her specialist subject and came third in the episode.
She spent about 100 hours making the moquette-inspired garment as a labour of love.

title: Third day of Tube disruption amid 'toxic air' from huge blaze near Wembley Stadium
author: Matt Watts
content:

Huge plumes of smoke could be seen in the sky in videos posted on social media, with firefighters still battling the blaze into the evening.
It is understood poor air quality has made it unsafe for trains to run on the Metropolitan line tracks near where the fire took place, while the level of “toxic air” is also preventing any TfL staff entering a train depot nearby to bring more trains into service.

The London Fire Brigade are continuing to investigate the fire.
summary: London Underground services on the Metropolitan line have suffered a third day of disruption due to poor air quality and toxic smoke from a large fire near Wembley Stadium. Meanwhile, Chiltern Railways services have returned to normal, and the London Fire Brigade continues to investigate the blaze.
key_points: Tube disruption on the Metropolitan line entered its third day due to a major fire near Wembley Stadium.
Toxic air and poor air quality made it unsafe for trains to run and prevented staff from entering a nearby depot.
Chiltern Railways services have returned to normal following the disruption.
The London Fire Brigade is continuing to investigate the cause of the fire.

title: Police arrest 169 at Notting Hill Carnival but mood ‘overwhelmingly positive’
author: Rosie Shead
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/20/8970309dd529c3d6190d32f4a529b9acY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4MjA0NTI0-2.85693927.jpg?crop=8:5,smart&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000)
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/20/a79a11a93ae55a8cdac8d577d6fd75ecY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4MjA0NTc3-2.85695051.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
In a statement on Sunday evening, the Met Police said: “While officers responded to a number of incidents as would be anticipated at an event of this scale, the mood has been overwhelmingly positive and celebratory.”
The force said the majority of arrests had taken place within the event perimeter and officers had responded to two knife assaults, a slashing to the leg and one to the hand, neither of which resulted in life-changing or threatening injuries.
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/20/fdd3b22500728aa254901069d336d94eY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4MjA0NjE5-2.85694096.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Commander Claire Smart, who is in charge of the policing operation, said: “We have been working closely with Notting Hill Carnival Ltd and other partners for many months ahead of this weekend’s event.
“The organisers have stepped forward significantly across the event, including crowd management, and we have seen the positive progress today.
“While we have seen a significant number of arrests and interventions by officers, the result of that proactive approach is a welcome reduction in the levels of serious violence seen at the event in previous years.
“Nobody involved in the delivery of the event is complacent, however.
“There are still many officers deployed across the footprint to ensure crowds disperse safely.
“We will have officers on duty through the night and tomorrow we will go again to ensure we can continue to tackle the minority who want to come to Carnival to spoil the celebration for the majority.”
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/20/501b784967d2717c6129ca1eb545d6ffY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg4MjA0NjUz-2.85692400.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Earlier this week, the force said more than 7,000 officers would be deployed to west London over the bank holiday weekend.
The carnival includes parades, live music, street food and sound stages and is celebrating its 60th anniversary this year.
In 2025, the Met said it made 528 arrests across the two main days of the carnival, including 167 for drug offences, 50 for possession of an offensive weapon, 21 for sexual offences, four for violence with injury and 49 for other violence.
In 2024, there were eight stabbings, including the murder of 32-year-old mother Cher Maximen, with the same number the previous year, and seven including a murder in 2022.
Day two of this year’s event is set to take place on bank holiday Monday.
summary: Police arrested 169 people during the Notting Hill Carnival, which is celebrating its 60th anniversary. Despite the arrests and incidents involving knife assaults, the Met Police described the overall mood as overwhelmingly positive and celebratory. Officials noted a reduction in serious violence compared to previous years due to proactive policing and improved crowd management.
key_points: Police made 169 arrests during the event, with the majority occurring within the carnival perimeter.
Officers responded to two knife assaults involving non-life-threatening injuries.
More than 7,000 officers were deployed to west London for the bank holiday weekend operation.
Organizers and police reported a welcome reduction in serious violence compared to previous years.

title: 'World class' London graffiti artist Helch 'dies' as tributes paid from art world
author: Shaun Wilson
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Appeal to find graffiti artist who scrawled 'I farted in yoga' on west London wall](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/30/15/51/helch.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
Graffiti artist Helch - who was behind some of the most famous outdoor murals in London - has reportedly died.
The guerrilla artist, whose real name is unknown, has gained a reputation for painting giant block words over buildings, concrete motorway bridges and rail viaducts as well as several rooftops.
Helch first came to prominence in 2018 by painting his eponymous tag 'Helch' in capital letters across a string of public spots in London as well as bridges on the M4, M1 and M25.
The tag was sometimes painted in stylised fonts or different colours, and occasionally appeared just as the simple letter 'H'.
Helch’s antics did not always go down well with the public, with some motorists hitting out in anger in October 2018 when an old graffiti sign of ‘Give Peas A Chance’ was replaced on the Chalfont Viaduct on the M25 with ’Give Helch A Break’.
But across the art world, Helch’s adventurous forays - usually carried out in the dead of night - led to him being dubbed “a world class artist” who “embodied everything we love about graffiti”.
In an online tribute, Alternative London posted: “We were so fortunate to witness him at work. We’ve never seen anyone do what he did before and there will never be another like him again.
“Above all he was a great human being who recently donated a share of his book sales to animal charities.
“Sending all our love and condolences to his family and loved ones. The streets of East London will never be the same again.”
News of Helch's death was shared on Instagram by BSMT space, an urban art gallery situated in Dalston, East London.
Read More
The gallery wrote online: "Receiving news today of the untimely passing of Helch has left us broken hearted. It felt like he stepped into our lives out of the ether.
"Prompted by a moment of revelation standing outside of the American Carwash in Shoreditch- a triumph of roller graffiti and an East London landmark- I was so drawn to the enigma and mystery of the word I had to find out more.
"It took six months to get him to agree to meet in person, and in 2022 we released his first print which sold out within the hour.
"A stranger to the gallery world Helch was a true creature of the night, it’s where he found his vocation and the gallery walls were not always what it was about for him. We often had to recalibrate what this meant as we worked together.
"Over the past year his work progressed exponentially, he was coming into his own as an artist. A true perfectionist- he wouldn’t present anything that wasn’t to his standard and it was an honour to witness.
"An urban landscape without an H in it seems unfathomable. A life unlike any other, he was compelled to leave his mark on this world. There will never be another like him. Rest well H- your rollers have spoken their truth."
Helch’s death has not been confirmed on his website.
summary: Renowned London guerrilla graffiti artist Helch has reportedly died, with tributes pouring in from across the art world. Operating under an unknown identity, Helch became famous for painting giant block words on prominent public buildings, bridges, and rooftops since 2018. Urban art gallery BSMT space and other admirers shared heartfelt tributes online, celebrating his unique artistic legacy.
key_points: Graffiti artist Helch, known for giant block-letter murals across London, has reportedly died.
He first gained widespread prominence in 2018 by painting tags on public spots and motorway bridges.
The art world praised him as a world-class artist with a unique approach to street art.
News of his passing was shared on Instagram by the Dalston-based urban art gallery BSMT space.

title: The 15 best new London restaurants opening in September 2026
author: Leonie Cooper
content:
[title]
Most of the UK restaurant industry took their August 9 to 5 off, and who can blame them? But the summer lull is now over and we’re heading into autumn with a bumper month of terribly exciting new openings for London.
We hope you’re feeling hungry, because not only does September herald the return of the king (aka Mangal II’s Sertaç Dirik), but a brand new gastropub from Public House Group – the hotshot squad behind Notting Hill’s bougie Fat Badger and Maida Vale’s The Hero.
There’s also a fresh kitchen residency at one of east London’s best pubs, The Adam & Eve, as well as the arrival of a Soho location for one of the best smashburgers around, Dumbo, and a new temporary home for Malaysian pop-up Duda Diner.
The best new London restaurants opening in September 2026
![Chef Sertaç Dirik and restaurateur David Carter of Kid](https://media.timeout.com/images/106416600/image.webp) 
1. The big one
KID, Soho
It’s hard to argue with the kitchen clout of Mangal II’s saviour aka chef Sertaç Dirik and Oma kingpin David Carter. Since Sertaç left the family business a couple of years ago, baby we’ve been burning for the announcement of his very own restaurant and it’s finally here. The dashing duo are opening Turkish restaurant Kid in the middle of town, promising magnificent meze and serious salatas, as well as the titular braised kid goat and köfte of many colours.
Opens: September 1
Address: 53-55 Frith Street, Soho, W1D 4SJ
![Casette](https://media.timeout.com/images/106441078/image.webp) 
2. The French Peckham transplant
Cassette, Covent Garden
The team behind Peckham’s lovely Levan and equally nice Bar Levan are heading central. On the south side of Covent Garden, this French restaurant will see former Planque chef Essa Fakhry leading things in this Grade II building from the 1630s. You’ll fall head over high heels for it. Levan co-owner Mark Gurney says: ‘It’s inspired by lazy weekends drinking gentian spritz and playing pétanque outside Auberge de Chassignolles; by Édouard at Bistrot des Tournelles in Paris, where our friendship grew over a shared love of music; and by Toto at Le Verre Volé, where I recently DJed as part of their Beaujolais Nouveau celebrations’.
Opens: Late September
Address: 42 Maiden Lane, Covent Garden, WC2E 7LJ
![Elliott Kaye of Marrion's Bar](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440793/image.webp) 
3. What Norman’s did next
Marrion’s Bar, Hackney
Only the memory of Norman’s remains, the new-school greasy spoon in Archway that people couldn’t quite work out if they loved or hated. Now the caff’s ole handy man Elliott Kaye (who’s also cooked at Lyle’s, The French House and Leroy) is back with a chilled-out east London bistro. Marrion’s Bar will serve up good wine and comfort food, with the likes of devilled crab rarebit, moules frites, a cheeseburger and tuna melts. ‘I wanted Marrion’s to be somewhere I’d actually want to go - somewhere you can have a drink, eat something good and feel at home. Nothing too fussy or pretentious,’ says Elliott.
Opens: September 10
Address: 177 Morning Lane, Hackney, E9 6LH
![Bunso](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440797/image.webp) 
4. The combination Filipino bakery and pizza joint
Bunso, Kentish Town
Hungry again? Bunso is the latest from Kentish Town hospitality kingpin Omar Shah. Hot on the heels of his breakout success Belly (not to mention Guanabana, Mamasons and Ramo Ramen), Bunso promises to be a Filipino bakery during the day before morphing into a pizza joint in the evenings. ‘I want Bunso to be somewhere you can come in the morning for a really good pastry and coffee, drop in for lunch, or come back at night for pizza, pasta and a bottle of wine,’ says Shah. ‘Ultimately, I want it to feel like it belongs to the neighbourhood.’
Opens: Late September
Address: 1a Hawley Road, Kentish Town, NW1 8RP
![Nakimushi](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440799/image.webp) 
5. Oodles of noodles
Nakimushi, Notting Hill
From the team behind Notting Hill’s acclaimed Dorian and Eel Sushi comes the grand Nakimushi, which will feature a ground-floor ramen bar and a more refined 25-seater upstairs restaurant serving a broader spectrum of Japanese cuisine. Chefs Yuji Shimokawa Kelly and Robin Kosuge gave both concepts successful trial runs at their Urchin and Robin's Ramen residencies at Holland Park’s Supermarket of Dreams, so expect a giddy and receptive audience as well as a busy signal when trying to book a table.
Opens: September 7
Address: 7 Kensington Mall, London, W8 4EB
6. The very posh pub
The Horses, Clerkenwell
With west London’s Fat Badger, Pelican and Hero as well as the Bull in Charlbury, Public House Group have finessed the art of the modern gastropub; putty-coloured plaster walls, artsy foxed mirrors and buffed wood finishes. Oh and extremely good cooking. The Horses is their first move east, and will bring their seasonal, Cotswolds-grown produce to the table. After something fishy? There’ll also be a host of seafood here at this former site of the 1897-built Coach & Horses.
Opens: Late September
Address: 26-28 Ray Street, Clerkenwell, EC1R 5ER
![Macbeth x Hot Fresh Pizza](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440801/image.webp) 
7. The Portuguese pizza spesh
The Macbeth x Fresh Hot Pizza at The Fox, Haggerston
What’s a monthly London restaurant update without a little pizza news, eh? This isn’t a new parlour but rather a week-long pop-up that brings together two local heroes; the revamped Macbeth’s Portuguese kitchen and the team behind Fresh Hot Pizza at the also newly revamped Fox. What happens when you bring them together? A pizza that pays tribute to Porto’s wet and wild Francesinha sandwich, dripping with mozzarella, and with sausage, ground beef and pork belly bobbing about like islands in the stream of cheese.
Available: August 31 to September 6
Address: 372 Kingsland Road, Haggerston, E8 4DA
![InterStellar BBQ](https://media.timeout.com/images/106436078/image.webp) 
8. The Michelin star BBQ takeover
InterStellar BBQ x La Barbecue at The Ned, City
American meat institutions InterStellar BBQ and La Barbecue are coming to London for a serious BBQ collaboration. Two of the best little smokehouses in Texas, these Michelin-recommended Austin spots are popping up at The Ned for a one-month residency, with pitmasters John Bates and Ali Clem prepping the ‘ultimate BBQ tray’, featuring peach tea glazed pork belly, pulled lamb shoulder, chimichurri beef short rib, pork ribs and chopped cheese sausage. Unbuckle your belts now in preparation.
Available: September 4 - October 4
Address: Electric Bar & Diner, The Ned, 27 Poultry, City, EC2R 8AJ
![Seouls of Mischief](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440804/image.webp) 
9. The punchy pub kitchen
Seouls of Mischief at The Adam & Eve, Homerton
Mexican-Korean fusion street food folk Mexican Seoul are giving their burger-based off-shoot Seouls of Mischief a spin at east London boozer, the Adam & Eve. Come for the smash burgers and wings as well as the elote corn ribs and stay for the weird ‘L’ shaped pool table. But try not to drink so many pints that you have to call ‘daddy come and get me’.
Launches: September 4
Address: 155 Homerton High Street, E9 6AS
![Beefbar](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440805/image.webp) 
10. The flash hotel resto revamp
Beefbar at Broadwick Soho, Soho
Broadwick Soho’s in-house restaurant is starting over again and ditching their Dear Jackie basement restaurant and replacing it with a branch of glitzy global brand Beefbar. The Chelsea outpost, Le Petit Beefbar, closed earlier this year in preparation. Expect this to be as razzle-dazzle as the Monte Carlo, Paris, Mykonos and New York outposts, with Japanese Kobe and Australian Wagyu served in an outré room, where everything’s beautiful in its own way.
Opens: September 14
Address: 20 Broadwick Street, Soho, W1F 8HT
![Pizzas on the menu at Five Feet](https://media.timeout.com/images/106432267/image.webp) 
11. Pan pizza perfection
Five Feet, Bermondsey
More pizza news! Five Feet Pizza comes from three heavyweights of the London food scene: Jay Patel (co-founder of Legare and Luna), Roland Horne (founder and CEO of WatchHouse) and Jack Ellingham (former chef and baker at Dusty Knuckle). They’ll be serving pan pizzas with spongy centimetre-thick dough (not quite thick enough to qualify as deep-dish). So powerful it might make your false eyelashes fall off.
Opens: September
Address: 4 Tanner Street, Bermondsey, SE1 3LE
![Duda Diner](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440806/image.webp) 
12. Malaysian magic in west London
Duda Diner at The Pilgrim, Paddington
After coming to the end of their Nunhead residency, Hakeem and Zura Ahmad of Duda Diner bring their superior nasi lemak and kerabu salad to The Pilgrim as the final part of the hotel’s 2026 Incubator Kitchen Series. Ideal for date night with your potential new boy (or girl) friend.
Available: September 17 to late December
Address: 25 London Street, Paddington, W2 1HH
![DUMBO burger](https://media.timeout.com/images/106431601/image.webp) 
13. Serious smash burgers for Soho
Dumbo, Soho
Dumbo’s second London burger joint will serve the same sleek cheeseburgers and fries as their Bethnal Green Road location. The French-born brand’s double patty smash burgers are bulked out with gleaming American cheese as well as plump pickles and ketchup and mustard. Dumbo also offers a vegetarian ‘Earth burger’ option, as well as fries and nuggets. If you eat like a little bird, this one ain’t for you.
Opens: September 4
Address: 37 Berwick Street, Soho, W1F 8RS
![Avinash Shashidhara/Talli Queen](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440811/image.webp) 
14. An Indian gastro-boozer
Talli Queen, Shepherd’s Bush
Former River Café cook and Pahli Hill head chef Avinash Shashidhara is opening a slick desi gastropub on the site of what was the Queen Adelaide pub. The menu will include ‘Military canteen-style meatballs’, chicken and liver pepper fry, Kerala chilli beef and Bangalore-inspired dosa. There’ll be roasts every Sunday, with slow-cooked lamb shoulder and biryani to share. With a great bar, there’ll be no reason to hurry home.
Opens: September
Address: 412 Uxbridge Road, W12 0NR.
![Rack City Ribs](https://media.timeout.com/images/106440813/image.webp) 
15. Soul food BBQ
Rack City Ribs at Kitchen E20, Stratford
Something’s burning? Nope, it’s just the excellent Rack City Ribs, previously in residence at north London honky tonk the Dukes of Highgate. They’re now swinging over to Kitchen E20 at the Stratford Hotel for a three month pop-up. Expect Caribbean-edged barbecue, with crispy jerk pork ribs, battered boar sausage and chicken wings with pineapple glaze.
Launches: September 1
Address: The Stratford Hotel, 20 International Way, London E20 1GQ
